mission_10: GAN-based data augmentation represents the cutting edge of synthetic data generation. Generative Adversarial Networks learn the underlying data distribution through an adversarial game between a generator that creates synthetic samples and a discriminator that distinguishes real from fake. Once trained, the generator can produce unlimited realistic samples that capture the statistical properties of the original data. This approach is particularly valuable when real data is scarce, expensive to collect, or contains sensitive information. GAN-augmented datasets have been shown to improve model performance across classification, segmentation, and detection tasks. The key challenge lies in training stability and mode collapse, but modern techniques like Wasserstein GAN and spectral normalization have made GAN training more reliable.
